direction.name: Miniature Factory Slapstick
direction.visual_spine: One locked top-down cardboard factory, one center conveyor, the real old video as a physical product tile, paper prop labels, green machine confidence, and one red human rejection state.
direction.text_contract: All words are attached to physical factory props; no overlay titles, captions, quote cards, or simulated UI.

references.borrow: Immediate artifact, stable spatial stage, compressed object-led changes, and a decisive audio turn.
references.avoid: Copied UI or audio, unsupported claims, and presenting any recreation as a live capture.

references.borrow: Traceable source evidence and visible self-critique.
references.avoid: Using generated atmosphere or actor props as factual proof.

scenes.title: The factory approves; the human drops it
scenes.purpose: Express the gap between measurable QA and human acceptance as one readable physical cause-and-effect gag.
scenes.entry_visual: The full miniature factory and the actual old video playing inside a paper product tile are visible at frame zero.

beats.visual: Complete factory; real source video already plays inside a product tile at the bottom of the center conveyor.
Product tile starts traveling up the fixed center belt.
The 1080P checkpoint flashes green as the scan sound lands.
The 60 FPS checkpoint turns green while the tile continues on the same axis.
A heavy physical PASSED stamp lands on the product tile.
Three small paper scraps pop from the machine and settle; the product keeps moving.
The same product tile reaches the HUMAN REVIEW bay and the paper hand enters from above.
The hand touches the red control; the trapdoor latch releases while the music stops sample-hard.
The trapdoor rotates open beneath the still-approved product tile.

motion.continuity_anchor: The product tile stays centered on the same conveyor axis while the trapdoor opens underneath it.
motion.why_not_static: The punchline depends on seeing the human action cause an immediate physical consequence.
motion.movement_envelope: Trapdoor plane rotates on its upper X hinge from 0deg to 82deg inside x=232..848 and y=780..1240; no text is carried on the rotating face.

beats.visual: The video product tile falls into the center opening; PASSED remains visible during the first half of the fall.
The product is gone and the red physical NOPE stencil is fully readable inside the chute.
Factory, open chute, still hand, and NOPE remain motionless in silence.

custom_motion_contracts.movement_envelope: Product tile center travels only on x=540, from y=1540 to y=850; its 560x315 bounds stay within x=260..820 and outside the bottom 180px delivery-safe zone after frame 9.
custom_motion_contracts.why_not_static: Continuous travel makes the three approvals read as one factory process rather than three slides.

custom_motion_contracts.movement_envelope: Alpha hand translates 300px downward within x=585..1035 and y=-340..850; it never overlaps the QA labels or the NOPE stencil.
custom_motion_contracts.continuity_anchor: product tile at the review bay
custom_motion_contracts.why_not_static: The entrance identifies a new actor without cutting away from the factory.

custom_motion_contracts.movement_envelope: Product tile stays between x=300..780, translates 230px downward, scales from 1.0 to 0.22, and disappears behind the chute mask before touching the NOPE stencil.
custom_motion_contracts.why_not_static: The visible fall is the comic consequence and cannot be replaced by an unexplained before/after inside the preferred signature scene.

states.visual: real product tile enters complete factory
three green checks and PASSED stamp

fallback_contract.story_preserved: real artifact, machine approval, human interruption, physical rejection, and final NOPE

scenes.music_cue: Reuse the selected Dry Acoustic Deadpan cue through audio/final-mix.m4a; scan at 0.700s, stamp at 3.150s, then sample-hard stop plus latch clunk at 4.600s and silence to 8.000s.
